title: Assignment 1: Obstacle Avoidance: Bug Algorithm Scenario 1
description: Calculate a true Bug2 m-line route with valid hit and leave points.
assignment_html:
Scenario

Purpose: Practice dividing a valid Bug2 path into approach, boundary-following, and departure distances.

A cleaning robot starts at S = (2, 1) and travels toward G = (8, 9). The straight start-to-goal line is the Bug2 m-line. A rectangular obstacle occupies 4 <= x <= 7 and 3 <= y <= 6.

  • Hit point: H = (4, 11/3), where the m-line first reaches the obstacle.
  • Clockwise boundary waypoint: T = (4, 6), the top-left corner.
  • Leave point: L = (23/4, 6), where the boundary meets the m-line again.
  • Required route: S -> H -> T -> L -> G.

H and L both lie on the m-line, and L is closer to G than H. Therefore, the robot may leave the boundary at L.

Task

Complete calculate_bug2_route(start, hit, corner, leave, goal). It must return four values in this order:

  1. Euclidean distance from start to hit.
  2. Boundary distance from hit through corner to leave.
  3. Euclidean distance from leave to goal.
  4. Total of the three traveled components.

distance = math.sqrt((x2 - x1)**2 + (y2 - y1)**2)

This is Euclidean (straight-line) distance. In Python, **2 means square; ^ is not exponentiation. The supplied calculate_distance(point_1, point_2) helper uses the equivalent math.hypot(dx, dy). For example, (0, 0) to (3, 4) has distance 5. Use the helper for each required segment, not as a shortcut across an obstacle.

Rules

  • Use the points passed into the function; do not hard-code the displayed answer.
  • Follow only hit -> corner -> leave; do not use the full obstacle perimeter.
  • Return exactly four numeric values in the required order.
  • The grader checks the displayed scenario and additional coordinate sets.
  • Code runs in a restricted Python sandbox. Use math or basic numpy functions, and f-strings for printed formatting. str.format, dict.update, math.pow, np.hypot, np.argmin, names that start with an underscore (including _), and file or system modules are not available.

Scope and scoring

You are calculating a supplied route, not implementing the Bug2 hit/leave decision or controlling a simulated robot. Each point is an (x, y) pair measured in the same distance units. The helper calculates the distance between two points; your route function combines the required segments.

  • Each of the four returned components is worth 25%. A component earns credit only when it is correct for every grading scenario, not just the displayed map.
  • Partial work can earn 25%, 50%, or 75%. Syntax errors, runtime errors, or an invalid return count must be fixed before calculations can be evaluated.
  • Return exactly four numeric values in the stated order. Do not round intermediate calculations or returned values. You may round only the printed display.
  • Run tests shows your score and feedback. AI tutoring is optional, off by default, and cannot change your grade.

Before you run the tests

  • Call your function with a second small example of your own.
  • Confirm that the total equals the other three values added once.

import math

start_point = (2.0, 1.0)
goal_point = (8.0, 9.0)
hit_point = (4.0, 11.0 / 3.0)
top_left = (4.0, 6.0)
leave_point = (23.0 / 4.0, 6.0)

# Euclidean (straight-line) distance; hypot(dx, dy) = sqrt(dx**2 + dy**2).

    return math.hypot(point_2[0] - point_1[0], point_2[1] - point_1[1])

learning_objectives: Use supplied Bug2 hit and leave points that lie on the start-to-goal m-line.
Calculate Euclidean path segments with fractional coordinates.
Decompose a Bug2 route into approach, boundary-following, and departure phases.
Explain from the scenario why L is a valid Bug2 leave point: it lies on the m-line and is closer to the goal than H.

rubric.description: Calculate the Euclidean distance from S to the valid hit point H.
Add both specified boundary segments from H through T to L.
Calculate the Euclidean distance from L to G.
Add the three traveled phases exactly once.

common_misconceptions.description: Uses Manhattan distance or a rectangle corner instead of the m-line hit point.
Omits a boundary segment or measures parts of the rectangle that the robot does not travel.
Starts the final segment at the corner instead of the stated m-line leave point.
Omits or double-counts one of the three traveled phases.

tutoring_rules.tone: Socratic, encouraging, and precise about Bug2 geometry

criteria.success_feedback: The start-to-hit distance works for every tested route.
criteria.failure_feedback: Use both coordinate differences when calculating the Euclidean distance from start to hit.

criteria.label: Boundary-following distance
criteria.success_feedback: The two boundary segments work for every tested route.
criteria.failure_feedback: Add hit-to-corner and corner-to-leave; do not use the full obstacle perimeter.

criteria.label: Departure distance
criteria.success_feedback: The leave-to-goal distance works for every tested route.
criteria.failure_feedback: Calculate the Euclidean distance from the supplied leave point to the supplied goal.

criteria.label: Complete route distance
criteria.success_feedback: The complete Bug2 route total is consistent.
criteria.failure_feedback: The total must equal the correct approach, boundary, and departure distances added exactly once. Fix any incorrect component first.

solution_html:
1. Reach H

The m-line distance from S to H is 10/3 units.

2. Follow the clockwise boundary

H-to-T is 7/3 units and T-to-L is 7/4 units, totaling 49/12 units.

3. Continue from L to G

The remaining m-line distance is 15/4 units.

Total path: 10/3 + 49/12 + 15/4 = 67/6, approximately 11.1667 units.
